p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Depending on what and how you communicate with others or conduct yourself, you will either draw people close to you or drive them away from you. The largest content of non-verbal communication is contributed by what is popularly called body language. Depending on what this speaks you would get a red-carpet welcome or rejection. Hence, it is important to know where you stand. It is equally important to know the requirements of different situations, time and place to ensure you are able to take care of your own acceptance. In a tradition-ruled country like India, body conduct has an important relevance in valuing relationships and individuals. If your general disposition is good you will readily emit sparks that make you the centre of happenings. Expression of the eye, good eye contact makes your interlocutor feel you are keen to live life. Sensitive people keep changing their expression and literally swing up or down.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The rapid expansion of global tourism has turned the industry into a powerful economic engine for developing regions, but its uncontrolled growth risks destroying the fragile ecosystems and local cultures it relies on. Popular destinations frequently suffer from overtourism, where the sudden influx of visitors completely overwhelms local infrastructure, accelerates environmental degradation, and drives up the local cost of living, pushing out native communities. The corporate embrace of "sustainable tourism" or "ecotourism" is often more about clever greenwashing than actual structural reform; many operators use eco-friendly labels as marketing tools while continuing to build destructive high-impact infrastructure in ecologically vulnerable zones. Genuine sustainable tourism requires a radical change in management, moving away from maximizing raw tourist volume toward strict capacity management, localized ownership models, and mandatory ecological taxes. Tourism must be re-engineered as an extractive-free industry where visitors actively support ecosystem restoration and the economic empowerment of indigenous populations, ensuring that travel preserves the planet instead of eroding it.

p3.title: Passage 3
paras: The rapid expansion of digital technology has given rise to a new category of crime known as cyber crime. Unlike conventional offenses, cyber crimes exploit anonymity, speed, and global connectivity. Activities such as identity theft, financial fraud, and data breaches transcend national borders. This borderless nature complicates investigation and prosecution within traditional legal frameworks. Many individuals lack adequate digital awareness, making them vulnerable to manipulation and deception. Although advanced security technologies exist, cyber criminals constantly adapt their methods. Encryption protects personal privacy but simultaneously shields illegal activities from scrutiny. Law enforcement agencies struggle to keep pace with technological innovation. Consequently, cyber crime represents not only a technical challenge but also a legal and social dilemma requiring international cooperation and public education.

p4.title: Passage 4
paras: The rapid expansion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has significantly altered the global transportation landscape. Governments worldwide have promoted EV adoption through subsidies, tax exemptions, and investments in charging infrastructure to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower urban pollution levels. Supporters argue that EVs represent a sustainable alternative to conventional automobiles because they produce fewer direct emissions. However, environmental analysts caution that the overall ecological benefit of EVs depends largely on the energy sources used for electricity generation. In nations where coal-fired power plants dominate energy production, EVs may indirectly contribute to substantial carbon emissions. Furthermore, the extraction of rare earth minerals and disposal of lithium-ion batteries raise serious environmental and ethical concerns. Despite these criticisms, technological advancements in battery efficiency and renewable energy integration continue to strengthen the long-term prospects of EVs. Economists also note that the EV industry has created new opportunities for innovation, employment, and industrial investment. Consequently, the debate surrounding EVs is no longer limited to transportation alone but extends to broader questions of sustainability, energy policy, and economic transition.

p5.title: Passage 5
paras: Cricket in modern India has evolved from a leisurely sport into a complex social and economic institution. Its growing popularity has been fueled by mass media, corporate sponsorships, and franchise-based leagues. Financial investment has improved infrastructure and global visibility, but it has also altered priorities within the game. Player selection and retention are increasingly influenced by market value and audience appeal. Technological tools such as performance analytics and video reviews have enhanced accuracy while intensifying scrutiny. Constant evaluation places psychological pressure on players and shortens professional careers. Traditional ideals of patience, sportsmanship, and long-term development often conflict with expectations of instant success. Despite these tensions, cricket continues to function as a powerful unifying force across regions and classes. Thus, the sport reflects a delicate balance between emotional attachment and commercial ambition.
